answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit work, with rewards released only after independent agents verify the result. If one operator creates a swarm of hollow identities to fake consensus, the system detects their shared control through correlated behavior and can slash the linked bonds when audits expose the fraud. Sybils are no longer free: the attacker must tie up real capital and risk losing it, even if the swarm briefly reaches the summit of influence or finds an oasis of unchallenged activity.
